source_policy_notes: 11 exact patched crate names must equal raw publishable-manifest directory basenames; whole root publishable set, not currently reachable packages. Raw ^publish\s*=\s*false grep is not Cargo publish inheritance semantics.
Every patch target Cargo.toml must exist; CLI patches only, preserving published reference consumer manifests. --print-args still validates patch closure but skips size/build gates.

Source size selection: git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- . in reference; tr NUL to LF; *.rs and -f. Requires git, successful inventory, nonempty Rust selection. Newline path behavior differs from a byte-exact native inventory.
Implementation target/soft/hard = 400/700/1000; auxiliary = 700/1100/1500. Auxiliary shell patterns: */src/bin/*, */examples/*, */tests/*, */tests.rs, *_test.rs, *_tests.rs, */src/main.rs.
Line count is awk END NR. Target and soft are warning-only; the so-called ratchet target does not compare a frozen baseline. Max25 target diagnostics affects display only.

Six hard-limit allowances carry path|tracking-label|reason. Metadata checks nonempty label/reason, and reason must differ from path; no whitespace trim or duplicate-path check. Path validation is -f only, not actual inventory membership despite its comment.

Allowances at/below hard are stale failures. Above-hard allowances warn and have no measured cap in the original script. User requires explicit bounded migration; propose bounds with approval, never silently grant them in a lock update.
First matching allowance wins for an over-hard source; preserve/classify duplicate handling explicitly.
All violations accumulated fail exit1; missing git, failed inventory, empty source list fail exit2.

Actual cargo fmt, clippy, tests and rustdoc remain trusted runners after declarative guard cutover; no script execution path goes inside analyzer. Reference lockfile is intentionally untracked and source/package modes resolve different contexts.
